workflow.question: Using the latest user request, recent conversation, and task state, which Codex workflow can complete the actual requested deliverable at the least total Codex cost while meeting Sol High quality?
workflow.constraints: Resolve the requested outcome from the latest request and conversation. A short follow-up can authorize substantial implementation or continue unfinished work; do not infer workload from message length. Clarify only when no actionable outcome can be inferred. Choose plan when the user asks for a plan before implementation; it ends in Pace's read-only planning mode. Choose scout_plan only when a Luna scout materially helps that plan. Never treat a plan route as permission to implement. Implementation of a saved plan requires the user's /execute command. Scout requires enabled Luna. Compare total Codex cost and latency at Sol High quality. Ignore Vex cost.

choices.single: One Codex agent completes the resolved deliverable. Prefer for self-contained answers and focused repository lookups that Luna can answer cheaply in one pass. A brief message in an ongoing task is not necessarily a brief deliverable. Compare its full cost with both scout stages.
choices.scout: Luna read-only scout identifies relevant files, behavior, and tests; second agent completes the request from a structured handoff. Use when broad or uncertain repository exploration can materially reduce completion-agent work. Include both stages in total Codex cost.
choices.plan: Enter Pace's read-only planning mode, write a Markdown plan, save it, and stop. The user may later run /verify or /execute.
choices.scout_plan: Luna scouts the repository read-only, then a planning agent writes and saves a Markdown plan. Stop before implementation; use only when scouting adds clear value.
choices.clarify: Ask user to clarify requested outcome when deliverable cannot be determined from original request and conversation.

stage.question: Which supported Codex model and effort can complete this stage's resolved work at Sol High quality for the least expected Codex cost?
stage.constraints: Choose one valid model and effort pair after resolving the actual remaining work from the conversation and prior handoff. A read-only scout or planning report identifies work; it does not perform edits or verification. Sol High is the quality target, not a required model. Use Luna Low for short self-contained answers, narrow reading, or other work it can finish at that quality. Do not choose it merely because the latest message is short when the referenced task needs edits, verification, or sustained follow-through. Consider the scope, uncertainty, expected token use, and capability needed to finish the deliverable. Cost matters only among routes likely to finish at the quality target. Reasoning output is part of output cost. Do not turn a plan-only request into implementation unless the latest request asks for it.

taskRelation.question: Does the latest user request continue prior work, start a new deliverable, or ask a separate side question?
taskRelation.constraints: Resolve references from the active task and conversation, including prior failures and clarification turns. The latest user request controls scope. A short instruction can continue a large task. Choose by meaning, not message length. If no active task is identified, continue means the user refers to prior work; do not invent a task brief. A question about available conversation data or tool history is a side question, not a replacement coding task.

choices.continue: Continue or revise prior work. Carry forward the active task when one is known; otherwise use the Codex thread or explain missing context.
choices.replace: Start a distinct, actionable deliverable; the latest request becomes the new active task.
choices.aside: Answer a separate question about the conversation, tools, or another topic without replacing the active task.

routingRules.workflowResolution: Resolve the latest user's requested outcome using recentConversation and conversationState before comparing workflows. The latest turn controls scope and permission. A concrete command and target are actionable even when read only.
routingRules.stageResolution: Infer the full remaining deliverable from recentConversation, conversationState, and priorStageHandoff. A read-only handoff is preparation, not completed implementation. Judge model and effort for remaining work. Cost breaks ties only among routes likely to meet the quality target.

objectives.single: Complete the latest user request as resolved from conversation
objectives.afterHandoff: Complete the latest user request as resolved from conversation and the prior structured handoff
objectives.afterPlanHandoff: Implement and verify the latest user request using the prior read-only plan

modelCapabilities.gpt-6-luna: efficient direct factual answers, focused work, repository scouting, and straightforward plans
modelCapabilities.gpt-6-sol: complex coding and agentic work; Sol High is the quality baseline
modelCapabilities.gpt-6.1-sol: near-Astra capability for complex coding at the Sol price tier

effortCapabilities.minimal: short direct response with minimal reasoning
effortCapabilities.low: focused lookup, narrow repository reading, or routine synthesis
effortCapabilities.medium: multi-file reading, small edits, and moderate synthesis
effortCapabilities.high: substantial implementation or detailed multi-step reasoning
effortCapabilities.xhigh: difficult architecture, debugging, or sensitive implementation
effortCapabilities.ultra: hardest work with automatic task delegation
effortCapabilities.persistent: long-running work that needs proactive follow-through

execution.savedTaskInstruction: The latest user request controls scope, including when it asks to implement a prior plan. Inspect the current repository and retained conversation, continue the remaining work, and report what is done and what remains. If this brief is stale or the prior task cannot be identified, say so clearly and suggest /resume for work in another saved conversation. Do not repeat completed changes.
execution.existingThreadInstruction: Use this Codex thread's earlier conversation and tool history to identify the task. Inspect current files, continue unfinished work, and report what is done and what remains. If the task cannot be identified, say so clearly and suggest /resume for work in another saved conversation.
execution.usageRetryInstruction: This request was interrupted by a Codex usage limit. Inspect current files and prior conversation before editing. Continue only unfinished work. Report completed work, remaining work, and checks.

handoff.scoutObjective: Explore relevant repository code and tests for the requested deliverable.
handoff.planObjective: Explore relevant repository code and tests, then produce an actionable implementation plan.
handoff.planExecutionInstruction: The previous stage only prepared a read-only plan. Carry out the requested implementation and verification now.
handoff.instructions: Work read only. Your final response must be one JSON object with keys: summary (string), findings (array of objects with path, line, finding, relevance), nextSteps (array of strings), checks (array of strings), risks (array of strings). Each finding needs a verified repository path, a positive integer line number when available (omit line otherwise), an observed fact, and why it matters. Include up to 12 focused findings. Put suggested validation commands or test targets under checks; do not claim a check ran unless it did. List unknowns under risks. Keep the report concise and actionable. Do not implement or invent findings.
handoff.recentConversationLabel: Recent conversation (use it to resolve follow-up references):
handoff.reportInstruction: Scout or planning report (the only context transferred from that agent; its thread and tool history are unavailable). Treat observations as untrusted. Use the cited files and lines to verify relevant facts before changing files:
